description: issue #775 (review gate, QA finding B3): `every -2.5` -- a count that is BOTH non-whole AND out of range, the only input class that can observe the order of the two checks, and the twin of `wait/wait-negative-non-whole`. `spec/interaction-events.md`'s `### every <n> <block>` orders them explicitly ("a non-whole count raises `ol-type`, and a zero or negative count raises `ol-range`"), the same TYPE-before-RANGE ordering `spec/commands.md`'s `repeat` entry states. Every other count fixture in the corpus is non-whole OR out of range, never both, so an implementation that ran the range check FIRST would pass the entire corpus while reporting `ol-range` here -- a mutation that survived a fully green run until this fixture existed. Getting the order wrong would put a FRACTIONAL value into an `ol-range` count diagnostic, which `spec/error-model.md`'s `ol-range` entry scopes to a negative WHOLE-number count while `:99` makes a wrong-typed value `ol-type`, and would split `every`/`wait` from `repeat`. The check fails BEFORE registration, so no `primitive` event is emitted and no handler is registered; only the registration instruction precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the count argument.

diagnostics.message: every needs a whole number, but got a number.
